title: This Alaska Lake Is Leaking Gas You Can Set on Fire
description:
Why does an Alaska lake bubble methane you can set on fire? Near Fairbanks, permafrost is thawing: ice wedges melt, the ground collapses into thermokarst ponds, and microbes turn long-frozen organic material into methane. At Big Trail Lake, emissions are about ten times higher than the rest of the Arctic's lakes and wetlands. NASA's ABoVE campaign tracks this thaw from the air with the UAVSAR radar.

In this episode:
0:00 A lake gas that burns
0:13 The frozen ground under Alaska
0:30 Inside the Permafrost Tunnel
0:47 Melting ice wedges and thermokarst ponds
1:16 NASA ABoVE and the UAVSAR radar
1:49 Fire, duff and the thaw cycle
